Explode pain drawings into multiple drawings by stroke

Source: R/pdr_explode.R
pdr_explode.Rd

Explodes each pdr_drawing into multiple pdr_drawings such that each stroke (as defined by the .strokes and .points elements of the drawing) becomes a new separate pdr_drawing.

Usage

pdr_explode(pdr_list)

Arguments

pdr_list

A pdr_list (see pdr_match()), e.g. the pdr_data column of a pdr_tibble.

Value

A pdr_list where each element is a pdr_drawing containing a single stroke from the input.

Details

NOTE The output of this function is (likely) not of same length as input.

For each input pdr_drawing:

  • Each row in .strokes becomes a new pdr_drawing

  • The matching rows (same .index) of .points are retained

  • The .id element is modified – see below.

The output is a pdr_list (see pdr_match()) with a different number of pdr_drawings than the input. The function is thus not suited for mutate() and similar functions which expect the same length of input and output.

Creation of id string

To ensure unique id strings for all pdr_drawings, the new .id has the format <index>_<id>_<stroke>, where <index> is the position of the input pdr_drawing in pdr_list, <id> is its original .id, and <stroke> is the stroke's .index. E.g. "2_abc_3".

Handling of missing or empty data

A pdr_drawing without strokes (.strokes is NA, NULL or has no rows) contributes no pdr_drawings to the result.

Examples

# Explode a pdr_list into one pdr_drawing per stroke
pdr_exploded <- pdr_explode(pdr_example_data$pdr_data[1:3])

# Number of strokes per original drawing vs. number of exploded drawings
sapply(pdr_example_data$pdr_data[1:3], \(d) nrow(d$.strokes))
#> [1] 2 6 7
length(pdr_exploded)
#> [1] 15

# The new ids have the format <index>_<id>_<stroke>
pdr_get_info(pdr_exploded, ".id")[1:5]
#> [1] "1_6d63804892233bbb18bc21bcf0d81d0d_1"
#> [2] "1_6d63804892233bbb18bc21bcf0d81d0d_2"
#> [3] "2_c8b12cd45d08e94241d4de9990d60f71_1"
#> [4] "2_c8b12cd45d08e94241d4de9990d60f71_2"
#> [5] "2_c8b12cd45d08e94241d4de9990d60f71_3"

# Each pdr_drawing now contains exactly one stroke
nrow(pdr_exploded[[1]]$.strokes)
#> [1] 1
